transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, I came in because my mind just won't hold onto things anymore. I'll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program—something I could do in my sleep before—and... the numbers and words just kind of scatter on me. I just can't seem to get my thoughts together.
When did you first notice that your memory and concentration started to get worse? Was it sudden, or did it come on gradually over weeks or months?
Well, it's been going on for about three weeks now. I suppose it wasn't really a gradual thing... it started right after my older sister died. Ever since then, it's just been like this.

You mentioned your sister died three weeks ago and your memory problems started right after that. Have you noticed any other changes in how you've been feeling since her death—such as feeling sad, empty, or losing interest in things you normally enjoy?

Yes, I suppose empty is a good word for it. Most days, I wake up with this... this heavy, hollow feeling right in my chest. It doesn't really go away. Even when my wife is sitting there, talking kindly to me, trying to reach me, I just feel like I'm sitting at the bottom of a well.
Besides the difficulty concentrating and memory problems, have you had any recent illnesses, head injuries, high fevers, or have you been taking any new medications in the past few weeks?
No, nothing like that. I haven't been sick, haven't hit my head or had a fever. And I'm not taking any new medications, just the same ones I've been on for years.
Have you ever experienced periods in the past where you felt this same kind of emptiness, heaviness, or loss of interest in things—before your sister passed away?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I've been sad before, like anyone else... but nothing like this. This heavy, hollow feeling, it's... it's new. I've never felt this way before she passed.

Besides the difficulty concentrating and memory problems, have you noticed any confusion, difficulty finding words, problems with your balance or coordination, or any other unusual changes in how your body or mind is working?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I can find my words fine, and my balance is normal. I don't feel confused, exactly... just that my memory isn't what it was, and it's hard to focus. But no problems with coordination or anything physical like you mentioned.

When you try to concentrate or remember things, does it feel like the problem is mainly that you're too sad and preoccupied to focus, or does it feel like something is actually wrong with your brain itself—like your memory just isn't working the way it should?

It feels more like my mind just will not hold onto things anymore. That's actually why I came in to see someone. I'll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program... something I could do in my sleep before. But now, the numbers and the words just scatter on me. So, yeah, it feels like it's just not working the way it should.
Have you actually made mistakes or forgotten important things at work or home that other people have noticed, or is it more that you feel like your memory isn't as sharp as it used to be?

Well, yes, people have definitely noticed. It's not just me feeling like I'm not sharp. I've... I've actually let a lot of things fall away completely. 

My church responsibilities, the garden... even that youth maker program. I just can't manage them right now. My wife and our pastor have actually had to step in and take over those things for me. And, well, I don't even go out to the workshop anymore. I just... I don't feel safe being out there by myself with the tools and everything when my mind is like this. So, yes, it's real things I'm dropping, and they definitely see it.
